abstract: The Japanese language contains a large class of compound words built on the morpheme *ki* (気) — including *denki* (電気, electricity), *jiki* (磁気, magnetism), *kibun* (気分, mood), *kimochi* (気持ち, feeling), *kehai* (気配, presence/atmosphere), and *genki* (元気, vitality). We propose that this linguistic structure is not accidental but reflects an implicit pre-scientific unification of physical and experiential phenomena under a single field concept — the Ki field (K_μν) of the Genki Particle framework.
